h1: The 8 Best Rolling Office Supply Carts Under $150 for Desks and Classrooms, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Office Supply Carts Under $150: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 8 rolling office supply carts under $150, from drawer carts to mobile file cabinets, compared on capacity, casters and build.
summary: The Liboocare 3-tier utility cart is the best office supply cart, with reinforced aluminum poles, polypropylene shelves and locking brakes on swivel casters. The MaxWorks cart handles heavy loads with a 225 pound maximum, the SUNALLY 8-drawer cart wins on small-item storage, and the IRIS 4-drawer unit moves easily between classrooms.
intro: The failure point of nearly every cheap rolling cart is the same, and it has nothing to do with the shelves or drawers. It is the wheels. Casters that look fine in the photo bind on a carpet, rattle on tile and, worst, skid when you push a loaded cart because they have no brake. If a cart is going to hold printer paper, files or craft supplies, the casters decide whether you use it or park it in a corner.

We reviewed eight carts under $150, ranging from open utility shelves to drawer towers and mobile file cabinets. They split by job: open carts for bulk items, drawer carts for small supplies and filing cabinets for documents. The ranking leans on load rating, caster quality, frame material and drawer design. Where a listing gives no weight capacity, we say so and treat that as a risk.

products.name: Liboocare 3-Tier Rolling Utility Cart with 2 Locking Brakes
products.verdict: Reinforced aluminum poles, polypropylene shelves and anti-tangle locking casters.
products.description:
The Liboocare is a 3-tier utility cart built with reinforced aluminum poles and durable polypropylene shelves. It rolls on four swivel casters with an anti-tangle design and two locking brakes, and measures 31.1 inches long, 16.5 wide and 37 tall. It sells for $50 to $100.

It wins on the details that matter: locking brakes keep the cart where you park it, the anti-tangle casters resist the hair and thread that jam cheap wheels, and aluminum poles do not rust. The compact footprint fits beside a desk or in a supply closet. It is the priciest in the ranking, but the build supports the cost.

Buy it as a general-purpose office cart for paper, printers and supplies. The listing gives no weight capacity.
pros: Locking brakes hold it in place
products.idealFor: General office use that needs a sturdy, brake-equipped cart.
products.skipIf: You need enclosed drawers for small items.

products.name: MaxWorks 80774 3-Shelf Utility Plastic Cart with Wheels-225 Lbs Maximum
products.verdict: A 225 pound rated utility cart with injection-molded shelves and rust-free legs.
products.description:
The MaxWorks 80774 is a 3-shelf utility cart rated for 225 pounds maximum, with injection-molded polypropylene shelves and aluminum legs that will not rust. It costs $50 to $100 and is designed for a wide variety of working environments.

Where it lands, second, comes down to the fact that it is the only cart here with a stated heavy load rating, which matters for reams of paper, boxes of files or small equipment. Molded polypropylene shelves resist stains and spills, and aluminum legs avoid rust in damp storage rooms. The tradeoff is that the listing does not mention locking casters, so a loaded cart may roll when you do not want it to.

Buy it for heavy supplies, a print room or a workshop-style office. Check the casters before loading it to the limit.
products.idealFor: Print rooms and heavy supply storage.

products.name: SUNALLY Rolling Cart With 8 Drawers,Storage Drawer Cart for Craft Art,Green
products.verdict: Eight spacious drawers on a powder-coated steel frame for $25 to $50.
products.description:
The SUNALLY is a rolling cart with 8 spacious storage drawers, built on a powder-coated steel frame, in green. It costs $25 to $50, the lowest tier in the ranking.

It places third because eight drawers sort small supplies, such as pens, tape, staples and craft items, better than any open cart can. The powder-coated steel frame resists chips and wear, and the price is hard to beat. Drawer carts typically have a lower weight limit than utility carts, and the listing gives none.

Buy it for desk supplies, craft materials or a teacher's classroom. Do not stack heavy reams or equipment on it.
products.idealFor: Small supplies, crafts and classroom storage.
products.skipIf: You store heavy or bulky items.

products.name: IRIS USA 4-Drawer Rolling Storage Cart with Organizer Top
products.verdict: Four drawers, an organizer top and removable wheels, with built-in drawer stops.
products.description:
The IRIS USA cart has four drawers, an organizer top and wheels that can be removed. The listing mentions built-in drawer stops that help prevent drawers from falling out, and it targets teachers and crafters. It costs $25 to $50.

The fourth spot follows because it blends practical details with a recognizable brand. Drawer stops stop the classic cart accident: yanking a drawer out and watching it crash to the floor. Removable wheels turn it into a stationary unit when you want, and the organizer top keeps pens and scissors at hand. It has fewer drawers than the SUNALLY.

Buy it for a classroom or home office where the cart moves occasionally. Choose the SUNALLY for more drawers.
pros: Organizer top for pens and scissors
products.idealFor: Teachers and crafters moving supplies between rooms.
products.skipIf: You need more than four drawers.

products.name: DEVAISE 3 Drawer Mobile File Cabinet
products.verdict: Three fabric drawers, a wide wood top and open shelves on four wheels.
products.description:
The DEVAISE is a 3-drawer mobile file cabinet with fabric drawers, a wide wood top, open storage shelves and four wheels, two of which lock. It costs $50 to $100.

Its fifth position rests on how it doubles as a small piece of furniture. The wood top gives you a surface for a lamp or printer, the open shelves hold binders, and the lockable casters keep it still. Fabric drawers are lighter than metal and quieter, but they are less sturdy under heavy files and may sag over time.

Buy it for a home office where looks matter. Do not rely on it for heavy file storage.
pros: Wide wood top as a surface
products.idealFor: Home offices that want a good-looking mobile unit.

products.name: Rolling Cart with Drawers
products.verdict: A metal storage cart on wheels with drawers that slide on premium tracks.
products.description:
This rolling cart has a reinforced metal frame, drawers that slide on tracks and wheels for moving it around. It is a storage cart priced at $50 to $100.

Rank sixth is a result of the fact that the metal frame and smooth tracks are good signs, but the listing gives no drawer count, capacity or caster details. A metal frame is stronger than plastic and resists warping, and tracks keep drawers from jamming. The brand is unnamed, which makes support uncertain.

Buy it if you prefer a metal drawer cart and can verify the dimensions. Compare it with the SUNALLY for clearer details.
products.idealFor: Buyers who prefer a metal drawer cart.

products.name: GYIIYUO 2 Drawer File Cabinet 24''W
products.verdict: A 24 inch two-drawer file cabinet with dual support, aimed at accountants and teachers.
products.description:
The GYIIYUO is a 24 inch wide, 2-drawer file cabinet with a tabletop surface, designed for accountants, teachers and tax pros. It uses dual support, with casters plus another feature, and costs $50 to $100.

Where it lands, seventh, comes down to the fact that it holds only two drawers' worth of files, yet it costs the same as larger carts. The tabletop surface and the dual support are good for a stable base while you work. The listing is truncated on how the support works, so confirm it before buying.

Buy it for a small mobile file station beside a desk. Skip it if you need a lot of storage.
products.idealFor: Small file stations for accountants and teachers.
products.skipIf: You need a lot of storage.

products.name: YASONIC 3 Tier Rolling Cart
products.verdict: A 100 percent metal three-tier cart at the low end of the price range.
products.description:
The YASONIC is a 3-tier rolling cart made entirely of metal, which the listing calls sturdy and durable, with multiple uses and easy installation. It costs $25 to $50.

The last spot follows because the listing is thin on dimensions, weight limit and casters. Metal carts are strong and resist cracking, but they can rust in damp rooms and are heavier to move. At the floor of the price tier, it is the cart to choose when budget is the main rule.

Buy it for a basic, low-cost utility cart. Check the load limit and caster quality.
products.skipIf: You want brakes and stated capacity.

methodology.title: Load rating and frame
methodology.description: We ranked stated weight limits, aluminum, steel and polypropylene construction, and marked down carts that list no capacity.

methodology.title: Casters and brakes
methodology.description: Swivel, locking and removable wheels were compared, since casters decide whether a loaded cart is safe to push.

methodology.title: Storage layout
methodology.description: Open shelves, small-item drawers and file drawers were matched to the job each is best at.

methodology.title: Footprint and mobility
methodology.description: Dimensions and ease of moving between rooms were weighed for desks, classrooms and closets.

methodology.title: Value under $150
methodology.description: Price tiers from $25 to $100 were compared against build, so the cheapest cart only ranks high when it does not cut corners.

whatMatters.detail: A ream of paper weighs about five pounds, so a few reams plus a printer approach 50 pounds quickly. Look for a stated maximum such as 225 pounds. Carts without a stated limit are risky for anything heavy.
Swivel casters turn easily, and locking brakes stop the cart from drifting when loaded. Anti-tangle designs resist hair and thread. Check that at least two casters lock.
Powder-coated steel resists chips, aluminum does not rust, and polypropylene shelves wipe clean. Plain metal can rust in damp rooms. Look for coatings or rust-free material on the listing.

Open shelves hold bulky items and show what you have, while drawers hide clutter and keep small things from falling. File drawers are sized for letter or legal folders. Choose by what you plan to store.
Measure the space where the cart will sit and the doorways it must pass. Most carts need simple assembly with a few screws. Check the dimensions and whether tools are required.

howToChoose.intro: Start with the stuff itself, since a cart built for paper reams is wrong for paper clips.

cards.label: Open shelves
cards.text: Hold bulky or heavy items and are easy to load. The Liboocare, MaxWorks and YASONIC carts use shelves.

cards.label: Drawers
cards.text: Hide clutter and organize small items. The SUNALLY, IRIS USA, DEVAISE and Rolling Cart with Drawers take this approach.

howToChoose.note: Choose shelves for bulk and heavy supplies, and drawers for small items you want tidy.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Drawers with stops, a compact footprint for classroom aisles and wheels that roll over thresholds. Light carts are easier to move between rooms.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The IRIS USA 4-Drawer Cart is built for classroom use, and the SUNALLY 8-Drawer Cart offers the most small-item storage.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You move heavy loads or share the cart in a busy office. The Liboocare and MaxWorks at $50 to $100 have the best build and ratings.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: The cart holds light supplies. The SUNALLY and IRIS USA at $25 to $50 will do.

faq.q: Can I use a utility cart for files?
faq.a: Yes, with file boxes or hanging folder frames. Open shelves hold boxes well. For hanging files, a mobile file cabinet like the DEVAISE is a better fit.

faq.q: What is the common mistake with cheap carts?
faq.a: Overloading shelves or drawers. Many carts have no stated limit, and overloaded casters fail first. Keep heavy items low and near the center.

faq.q: Is a metal cart worth it over plastic?
faq.a: For heavy loads, yes. Metal frames resist flexing. Plastic shelves like the MaxWorks and Liboocare are easy to clean and do not rust, so they suit damp rooms.
Most carts need simple assembly with a few screws or snap-fit parts. The MaxWorks has legs that are easy to install. Allow about 20 to 30 minutes.

faq.q: How do I keep casters rolling smoothly?
faq.a: Clear hair and thread from the wheels, and wipe the swivel with a cloth. Tighten the caster bolts every few months. Anti-tangle designs reduce buildup.

faq.q: Can the carts be used outdoors?
faq.a: Aluminum and polypropylene models resist rust, but check the manual. Metal carts can corrode if left in the rain. Store them indoors.

finalTake: The Liboocare 3-Tier Utility Cart is the best office supply cart, with locking brakes, anti-tangle casters and a rust-free frame. The MaxWorks 80774 is the choice for heavy loads, and the SUNALLY 8-drawer cart is the best for small items at $25 to $50. Pick the IRIS USA for classrooms, and the DEVAISE for a home office that needs filing.
